picks.title: Netflix says it's already used AI in 'roughly 300' titles this year
picks.excerpt: Netflix disclosed in its Q2 shareholder letter that generative-AI workflows were used in roughly 300 titles released or produced in 2026, concentrated in post-production (enhanced crowds, historical battle sequences, establishing shots). It named Glory (India), Brasil 70: A Saga do Tri and The American Experiment as examples, arguing the tools deliver higher-quality output faster and cheaper while human expertise stays essential.
picks.rationale: Hard scale signal from a major studio-buyer — AI post is now baseline across ~300 titles, reframing where VFX and post craft time actually goes; credible Engadget report on a fresh Q2 disclosure.

picks.title: Elon Musk claims Grok will make a 'historically accurate' Odyssey by the end of the year
picks.excerpt: Elon Musk says xAI's Grok Imagine will generate a full-length, 'historically accurate' film adaptation of Homer's Odyssey by year's end, framing generative text-to-video as a rival to Christopher Nolan's theatrical version. The sample footage shown so far has significant quality issues, making the claim a test of how far AI feature generation can actually go.
picks.rationale: Novel and freshest item — sets a public year-end benchmark for feature-length text-to-video against a Nolan release, a concrete stake-in-the-ground for how far gen-video craft is being pushed; distinct outlet keeps the set diverse.

picks.title: How Serviceplan MAKE Uses Luma to Put Creativity First
picks.excerpt: Case study: agency Serviceplan MAKE uses Luma's generative video to visualize concepts and deliver client-ready shots in a single day instead of multi-day studio production. The workflow shift moves time away from execution/post toward concept refinement and faster client feedback.
picks.rationale: Highest actionability — a concrete production-workflow case study that collapses multi-day studio shoots to same-day client-ready shots, directly changing how a craft team allocates time tomorrow.

picks.title: Meshy Wants AI to Feel Less Like a Prompt and More Like a Creative Partner
picks.excerpt: Meshy launched its 3D Agent Beta, a conversational AI that acts as a creative collaborator rather than a one-shot prompt tool, holding context across a session so artists can set a consistent art direction and generate stylistically unified families of 3D assets. It positions AI for early-stage concept exploration for film/VFX and animation pipelines while keeping artistic control with the creator.
picks.rationale: Actionable pipeline shift for film/VFX concepting — a context-holding 3D agent that keeps art direction consistent across an asset family, changing how previz and asset exploration is done; adds an under-represented tool/outlet to the set.
